theme: Source-linked histories of ancient settlements and living towns across South Asia
question: Which living towns have evidence of Indus-period habitation, and which have a demonstrated dated sequence connecting that occupation to the present settlement?
outcome: A register compares sixteen living-town or modern-settlement candidates in five countries with two abandoned Indus cities, using twenty-four source records. Harappa and Rupnagar have local Mature Indus overlap. Kenoyer's primary report documents the modern town over part of Harappa, while its post-1300 BCE dated bridge remains unresolved; Rupnagar's ASI card explicitly records a post-Harappan break. No complete source-audited Indus-to-present occupation sequence was found within the reviewed candidates. The register preserves nearby earlier sites separately and makes no exhaustive oldest-town ranking.
challenge: Municipal names, sacred places, nearby prehistoric sites and excavated mounds are often assigned one age. Some government routes timed out or failed legacy TLS, publication and reprint years differed, and one initial PDF locator was one page early.
remedy: Recorded the dated evidence place, modern civic identity, spatial relation, phase bounds, known gaps, access depth and source rights separately. Acquired public alternate primary scans, checked title pages and bounded chronology passages, preserved the failed locator check and wrote a corrected version. All raw witnesses and derivatives remain local-only on D:.
retry_when: New source-specific stratigraphy closes the c. 1300 BCE-to-historic gap beneath modern Harappa, locates Rupnagar occupation during its reported breaks, supplies independently checkable older dates at Vadnagar or Rajghat, or joins a modern settlement to its separately located early predecessor. Repeating tourist age lists or shifting a municipality's age from a nearby prehistoric site adds no sequence evidence.
